subject: Civil Engineering
title: Magnitude and Intensity Scales
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Magnitude and Intensity Scales.

hook.text: Magnitude measures the earthquake's energy. Intensity measures what people feel — they differ.

buildup.text: The moment magnitude scale (Mw) measures total energy released — it replaced the Richter scale.

discovery.text: Each whole number increase means 32 times more energy — magnitude 7 is 1,000 times a magnitude 5.

twist.text: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale rates shaking from I (not felt) to XII (total destruction).

climax.text: A magnitude 6 earthquake is devastating near the fault but barely felt 200 miles away.

punchline.text: Magnitude tells what happened. Intensity tells what you experienced.

quiz.question: How much more energy does a magnitude 7 earthquake release compared to magnitude 5?

details.summary: Earthquake magnitude measures the total energy released at the source using a logarithmic scale where each whole number represents a 32-fold energy increase.
details.whyItMatters: Magnitude and intensity serve different purposes. Magnitude describes the earthquake itself, while intensity describes its effects at a location, which is what engineers need for structural design.
takeaways: Magnitude is a single number describing total earthquake energy release
Intensity varies by location and depends on distance, depth, and soil conditions
Each magnitude unit increase represents 32 times more energy released

faq.question: Why was the Richter scale replaced by the moment magnitude scale?
faq.answer: The Richter scale was designed for Southern California using a specific seismometer type and saturated for large earthquakes, meaning it underestimated their true size.

faq.question: How can two locations experience different intensities from the same earthquake?
faq.answer: Intensity decreases with distance from the fault as seismic waves diminish. Soft soil amplifies shaking compared to rock at the same distance. Basin geometry can trap and amplify waves. Building vulnerability affects observed damage levels.
